page_title: "Instant Loading" with IndexedDB (Building a PWA, Part 2)

summary.title: "Instant Loading" with IndexedDB (Building a PWA, Part 2)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to store fetched data in IndexedDB using the idb Promise wrapper so a web app can show saved content instantly and refresh it from the network later.
keywords: how to store data in browser for offline use
takeaways: Open an IndexedDB database with idb.open and create object stores with a keyPath and optional indexes.
Wrap every CRUD operation in a transaction: open the DB, open a readwrite or readonly transaction, act on the store, then complete the transaction.
Show locally saved data first from IndexedDB, then fetch updated data from the network in the background for an instant-loading experience.
summary.summary: This is Part 2 of a three-part series on building an offline-first Progressive Web App for a blog. The article explains what IndexedDB is and walks through creating a database and object stores with the idb Promise wrapper, including keyPath and indexes. It then covers create/update, read, and delete operations as step-by-step transaction code examples. It finishes by showing how cached RSS articles are loaded from IndexedDB first and refreshed over the network afterward.
